title: Stamp 1: Grundgesetz and Federalism
welcome_lead: Stamp Germany's Basic Law and federal structure.
meta_desc: A-Level German adventure on the Grundgesetz, federalism, and the 16 Lander.

concepts.def: Basic Law of 1949, Germany's constitution since reunification.
Human dignity; Article 1 declares it inviolable as foundation of the Grundgesetz.
Federal system; powers shared between federation and 16 Lander.
Federal state; Germany has 16, each with its own parliament and government.
Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe, reviewing laws against the Grundgesetz.
Eternity clause; Article 79.3 protecting core principles from amendment.

walkthroughs.body_html: Drafted in 1948-49 by the Parlamentarischer Rat, the Grundgesetz was deliberately called provisional pending reunification. It became the constitution of unified Germany in 1990 without major changes.

Examples include Bayern (Munich), Nordrhein-Westfalen (Dusseldorf), Baden-Wurttemberg (Stuttgart), Sachsen (Dresden), and the city-states Berlin, Hamburg, Bremen. Each has a Landtag (state parliament).

The Bundesverfassungsgericht in Karlsruhe can strike down laws as unconstitutional. Citizens can file individual constitutional complaints (Verfassungsbeschwerde). Decisions bind all other courts and authorities.

mcqs.q: In 'Heute gehe ich ins Kino', why does 'gehe' come second?
options: Feminine.
German is a V2 language - the conjugated verb is the second element in main clauses.
Word order is free.
Heute is always followed by a verb.
